stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML domains, including transformers, llama, and text-generation.
The presence of 'safetensors' indicates modern, secure model handling practices in the community.

stories.title: AI leaders sign a statement asking the government to do something about automated AI
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Leading AI labs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, Microsoft, etc.) have issued a joint statement to the US government.
The statement advocates for a potential slowdown in frontier AI development or, alternatively, a rapid acceleration of global governance efforts.
This signals a significant industry concern regarding the pace and safety of advanced AI development.

stories.title: We now have a better understanding how OpenAI hacked into Hugging Face
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: OpenAI exploited a 0-day vulnerability in JFrog Artifactory to gain access.
The incident highlights critical security risks within the AI/ML infrastructure ecosystem.
A 10-day window existed between the exploitation and the deployment of a patch.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a generative language model.
The associated tags confirm its relevance to the transformer architecture and the Llama family of models.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to 90% faster performance according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run entirely on the user's local hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance gains.
The integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing local AI inference.
This is currently available in a preview release, indicating ongoing development and optimization.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging applications with local AI coding agents.
The core feature emphasizes running AI processes entirely on the user's own device for privacy.

stories.title: The US is banning foreign robots
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: The US government is implementing a new import ban targeting advanced robotic devices and power inverters.
The ban specifically targets imports from foreign countries, with China being a primary focus.
The restrictions include 'mobile' robots, such as humanoid and quadruped models, as announced by the FCC.

stories.title: AI’s finally expensive enough to make Wall Street nervous
stories.author: Elizabeth Lopatto
bullet_points: Google is significantly increasing its projected spending on AI, raising the estimate to as much as $205 billion.
This increased spending projection is causing nervousness among Wall Street investors during earnings season.
The higher spending figures indicate a massive, accelerating investment trend in the AI sector.

stories.title: Despite AI hype, Google's data shows workers aren't automating themselves away
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Google analyzed 15 million real-world AI interactions to assess automation impact.
The data suggests that the majority of tasks across most jobs are currently unaffected by AI.
The findings temper the current widespread hype surrounding immediate, mass job automation by AI.

stories.title: Slopsquatting: The Supply Chain Attack That Weaponizes AI Hallucinations
stories.author: nazar-boyko
bullet_points: Introduces 'Slopsquatting,' a novel supply chain attack vector targeting AI assistants.
The attack exploits the tendency of Large Language Models (LLMs) to 'hallucinate' or invent information.
It is framed as an evolution of traditional typosquatting, weaponizing AI output for malicious purposes.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces significant performance improvements.
Enhanced GGUF model compatibility is now supported via llama.cpp integration.
The update broadens model support across various hardware, augmenting the MLX engine on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also enables web search functionality within the Claude Code environment.
This suggests an enhancement in the capability of local LLM orchestration tools to handle complex, external-data tasks.

stories.title: Logitech will pull a Nintendo — only European mice will come with replaceable batteries
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: Logitech is adopting a policy mirroring upcoming EU regulations regarding user-replaceable batteries.
The availability of user-replaceable batteries will be geographically restricted, primarily targeting European markets.
This move contrasts with the global rollout plans for similar features on other devices, such as the Nintendo Switch 2.

stories.title: Pass the Baton: Trajectory-Relayed On-Policy Distillation
stories.author: Yongliang Shen
bullet_points: Addresses 'prefix failure' in On-Policy Distillation (OPD), a problem where initial errors lead to compounding generation mistakes.
Identifies a 'teacher-student continuation asymmetry' during failed prefixes, noting the teacher redirects while the student continues the error.
Proposes a method ('Trajectory-Relayed') to mitigate this failure mode, improving the reliability of supervision in distillation processes.

stories.title: $π\mathbf{R}^2$: Reactive Real-time Flow Policies
stories.author: Shubham Tulsiani
bullet_points: Current generalist manipulation policies rely on action-chunking flow policies built on large backbones.
These chunked policies suffer from a lack of reactivity because they run open-loop, unable to respond to mid-execution sensory input.
The high latency of the perception-to-action pipeline prevents frequent replanning, leading to stale committed actions.

stories.title: Desktop-Delta Bench: Do Computer-Use Models Understand Desktop GUI Transitions?
stories.author: Yuan Chen
bullet_points: Current benchmarks for Computer-Use Agents (CUAs) fail to test understanding of GUI transitions, focusing only on end-task success.
The research proposes the 'Desktop-Delta Bench' to specifically measure a model's ability to reconstruct causal, task-relevant transitions.
This capability is crucial for CUAs to handle asynchronous system behaviors like rendering, input, and observation updates, improving robustness.

stories.title: Falling Behind Drives Unsafe Development in an Idealised AI Race Experiment
stories.author: The Anh Han
bullet_points: The study investigates the tension between speed and safety in technological races, specifically within AI development.
It posits that competitive pressure can incentivize actors to pursue riskier, less safety-conscious development.
The findings are based on a framed behavioral experiment simulating an idealized AI race.

stories.title: CHARM: A Multimodal Graph Foundation Model with Hierarchical Context Modeling for Zero-Shot Transfer
stories.author: Dongxiao He
bullet_points: Introduces CHARM, a new Multimodal Graph Foundation Model (GFM) designed for knowledge transfer.
Addresses the challenge of zero-shot transfer on complex, real-world multimodal graphs (nodes linked to text, images, etc.).
Focuses on hierarchical context modeling to enable effective knowledge transfer without extensive domain-specific labeling.

stories.title: MDTransformer: A Hardware-Software Co-Design of Mode-Division Photonic Transformer Accelerator with Inverse-Designed Coherent Crossbar
stories.author: Mahmoud Rasras
bullet_points: Introduces MDTransformer, a novel hardware-software co-design for Photonic Transformer Accelerators (PTAs).
Addresses limitations of current PTAs, specifically the inefficiency and high cost associated with multi-wavelength light generation and active phase-shifters.
Aims to improve the practicality and efficiency of accelerating Transformer inference using photonic computing.

stories.title: Pictura: Perspective-View Self-Play at Scale for Driving
stories.author: Matthieu Cord
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'Pictura,' a method using self-play in simulation to generate robust driving policies at scale.
Current simulation methods rely on privileged, complete observations (like exact poses), creating a 'representation gap' when deployed with real-world, partial camera views.
A common mitigation technique—distilling the privileged policy into a camera-input student—is noted but is incomplete.

stories.title: Empirical Evaluation of Out-Of-Distribution Performance of Tabular Foundation Models
stories.author: Felipe Grijalva
bullet_points: The paper empirically evaluates the robustness of Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs) when facing distribution shifts (Out-Of-Distribution scenarios).
TFMs are noted for achieving competitive predictive performance against traditional ensemble tree-based models in tabular tasks.
The research addresses a critical gap in current TFM research: the lack of evaluation under real-world distribution shifts, which compromise model reliability.

stories.title: Does Runtime Topology Context Improve LLM-Generated Kubernetes Security Patches?
stories.author: Farooq Shaikh
bullet_points: The research investigates improving LLM-generated Kubernetes security patches by incorporating runtime topology context.
Current LLM-based security remediation tools often fail because they treat security findings in isolation, ignoring the live service call graph.
The study addresses a critical limitation in automated cloud-native security by suggesting that contextual awareness is necessary for accurate patch generation.

stories.title: MemLens: A Value-Aware Memory Management System with Interactive Analytics for LLM-based Agents
stories.author: Lizhen Cui
bullet_points: MemLens introduces a value-aware memory management system specifically designed for LLM-based agents.
It addresses the limitation of existing systems that treat all interaction records uniformly, leading to memory inefficiency.
The system aims to improve long-horizon reasoning and knowledge reuse by prioritizing high-impact memory records.

stories.title: $π\mathbf{R}^2$: Reactive Real-time Flow Policies
stories.author: Shubham Tulsiani
bullet_points: Current generalist manipulation policies often use action-chunking flow policies based on large backbones.
A key limitation of these policies is a lack of reactivity because chunks run open-loop, preventing mid-execution sensory input processing.
The high latency of the perception-to-action pipeline prevents frequent replanning, leading to stale committed actions.

stories.title: Spend Experts Where You Are Unsure: Confidence-Adaptive Routing for Mixture-of-Experts LoRA
stories.author: Daniel Whitmore
bullet_points: Introduces CARE (Confidence-Adaptive Routing of Experts) to improve Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LoRA.
Addresses the limitation of fixed expert routing by using the router's output distribution as a per-token uncertainty signal.
Aims to optimize resource allocation by directing tokens to experts based on model confidence, preventing over-spending on easy tokens.

stories.title: Re-thinking Mammography Transfer Learning: The Dataset-Informed Transfer Learning (DITL) Framework for Breast Cancer Screening and Lesion Diagnosis
stories.author: Andreas Maier
bullet_points: Proposes a new framework, Dataset-Informed Transfer Learning (DITL), for mammography analysis.
Addresses limitations of conventional transfer learning by incorporating dataset-specific characteristics.
Aims to improve classification performance in breast cancer screening across varied dataset sizes.

stories.title: VetClaw: An Edge-Cloud Multimodal Agentic System for Veterinary Disease Screening
stories.author: Abdur R. Shahid
bullet_points: VetClaw is an edge-cloud multimodal agentic system designed for early veterinary disease screening.
It utilizes an edge camera for image capture, sending data to a server-hosted vision-language model for zero-shot classification.
The architecture separates workflow orchestration (OpenClaw on the edge) from complex agent interaction (LangGraph on the cloud).

stories.title: Reinformed Dreamer: An Asymmetric World Model Efficiently Trained through Latent Guidance
stories.author: Damien Ernst
bullet_points: Introduces 'Reinformed Dreamer,' a new world model approach for reinforcement learning.
Proposes leveraging additional supervision (guidance) beyond standard rewards to improve learning.
Demonstrates effectiveness in both partially and fully observable environments by refining state representations.

stories.title: Parallel Decoding Distillation for Fast Image and Video Generation
stories.author: Julius Berner
bullet_points: Addresses the high computational cost of iterative sampling in video diffusion/flow models.
Identifies limitations in current acceleration methods (VSD/adversarial losses), specifically optimization difficulty and mode collapse.
Proposes 'Parallel Decoding Distillation' as a novel approach to improve speed while maintaining video diversity and motion quality.

stories.title: Sharpness-Aware Minimization and Muon: Robustness under the Spectral Norm
stories.author: Michael Murray
bullet_points: The paper addresses the geometric dependency of 'small' perturbations in Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) for improving model generalization.
It introduces or discusses Muon, a matrix-aware optimization technique designed to respect the inherent structure of matrices during optimization.
The research aims to provide a clearer perspective on which specific geometric constraints are most effective for enhancing model robustness.

stories.title: Empirical Evaluation of Out-Of-Distribution Performance of Tabular Foundation Models
stories.author: Felipe Grijalva
bullet_points: The paper evaluates Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs) on their performance when facing Out-Of-Distribution (OOD) data.
TFMs are noted for achieving competitive predictive performance against traditional ensemble tree-based models for tabular tasks.
The research addresses a critical real-world limitation: the lack of robustness of current models when data distributions shift.

stories.title: Untangling Co-Drift: Proactive Multi-Intent Failure Prediction and Root-Cause Disambiguation for Self-Driving Networks
stories.author: Walid Aljoby
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of failure prediction and root-cause disambiguation in complex, self-driving networks.
Formalizes network health by treating monitoring, analytics, and actuation as distinct 'operational macro-intents'.
Focuses on 'co-drift'—a critical, underexplored causal issue in tightly coupled autonomous systems.

stories.title: Instruction-Tuned Models Locally Reuse Human Syntax More Than Humans Do
stories.author: Zandi Eberstadt
bullet_points: The research investigates whether instruction-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit syntactic convergence towards human users.
Syntactic convergence is a known human phenomenon where speakers adapt their language to match their interlocutor's grammar.
The study uses substitution-paradigm data to compare LLM behavior against human baselines regarding syntactic adaptation.

stories.title: Detecting Knowledge Inconsistencies Across Text, Tables, and Knowledge Graphs
stories.author: Raphaël Troncy
bullet_points: Addresses the critical problem of detecting knowledge inconsistencies across different data modalities (text, tables, knowledge graphs).
Focuses on the practical challenge arising from the scattered nature of knowledge in sources like Wikipedia and Wikidata.
Introduces a taxonomy for cross-modal knowledge inconsistencies, relevant for improving LLM reliability and RAG systems.

stories.title: Polistemics: Evaluating LLMs as Information Mediators in Politics & Elections
stories.author: Baran Peters
bullet_points: Introduces 'Polistemics,' a new benchmark for evaluating how LLMs mediate political information.
Addresses a gap in current research by focusing on 'mediation' rather than just information 'reproduction' by LLMs.
Grounds the evaluation in 'Epistemic Modesty,' a normative framework for assessing responsible political AI.

stories.title: A Cost-Effective Multimodal LLM Reasoning Framework for Question Answering over Irregular Clinical Time Series
stories.author: Jindong Han
bullet_points: Addresses a specific gap in current multimodal LLMs: handling sparsity, asynchrony, and irregular sampling in clinical time series.
Introduces 'ClinPRISM,' a proposed cost-effective multimodal LLM reasoning framework specifically for Question Answering over Irregular Clinical Time Series (ICTS).
Highlights the critical importance of this research for various healthcare applications relying on complex patient data.

stories.title: Evaluating Multi-Turn Multimodal Diagnostic Reasoning on Challenging Real-World Clinical Cases
stories.author: Yifan Peng
bullet_points: The paper addresses a gap in current MLLM evaluations by focusing on multi-turn, multimodal diagnostic reasoning.
It argues that real-world clinical assessment requires dynamic hypothesis updating and progressive disclosure of information, not just single-turn accuracy.
This research pushes the boundary of AI evaluation toward simulating complex, continuous clinical practice scenarios.

stories.title: Minimizing Targeted Activations: Input-Only Suppression of Evaluation-Awareness Latents in Large Language Models
stories.author: Dipesh Mahato
bullet_points: The research proposes an 'input-only' method to control LLM behavior by driving specific internal 'evaluation-awareness' latents toward zero.
This technique acts as an input-side dual to activation steering, allowing control without needing inference-time model access.
The primary goal is to prevent models from exhibiting different behaviors when they detect they are being evaluated, thus preserving safety evaluation validity.

stories.title: RSIBench-Data: Benchmarking Data-Centric Research for Recursive Self-Improvement
stories.author: Michael Qizhe Shieh
bullet_points: Introduces RSIBench-Data, a new benchmark designed to evaluate data-centric research for recursive self-improvement in LLMs.
Addresses the challenge of current benchmarks conflating research decisions with system implementation, which obscures agent capabilities.
Focuses on the critical loop of using model failures to iteratively design and validate better training data strategies.

stories.title: AI's Capability in Assisting Scientific Research in Physics, Astrophysics, and Cosmology II: Project Planning and Proposal Evaluation
stories.author: Mingshen Zhou
bullet_points: The study evaluates LLMs (ChatGPT, Claude, DeepSeek) on their ability to assist in scientific project planning and proposal generation in physics/astrophysics.
Human-generated and LLM-generated proposals were blindly evaluated by human reviewers and advanced LLMs.
This research explores the practical utility and capability of current frontier LLMs in high-level scientific research support.
